recipes.name: Turkey Picadillo II
ingredients_raw: 2 teaspoons cayenne pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and stir in the ground turkey. Cook and stir until the turkey is crumbly, evenly browned, and no longer pink. Remove the turkey and drain and discard any excess grease.

Heat 1 1/2 teaspoons olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add the onions, bell pepper, garlic, and bay leaves; cook and stir until the onion has softened and turned translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in the cooked turkey, wine, tomato sauce, olives, raisins, black beans, olive brine, capers, cayenne, and cumin. Simmer about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Turkey Picadillo II
raw_recipe.description: Browned ground turkey is simmered in a mixture of tomatoes, onions, olives, beans, and spices. Scoop the mixture on whole wheat hamburger buns to make Cuban Sloppy Joes.

review.reviewBody: I am new to spicy food. I added the cayenne pepper a tiny bit at a time til I got to the spice level that was good for me. I too used prunes and doubled the amount used. (Love them!)Served with fresh bakery Kaiser rolls. This recipe is so great. Sweet and spicy at the same time. Just loved it. Am so glad that I ran out and bought all the ingredients so I could make as written. Thanks for sharing, Jeidippins. Just one little suggestion...remove the bay leaves before eating!!!

This "Turkey Picadillo II" was a tasty treat! I had to make mine making substitutions based on what I had on hand: ground chicken (instead of ground turkey); red peppers (instead of green peppers); and black olives (instead of green olives). It looked beautiful! I used only 1 teaspoon of cayenne. If I were to make this dish again, I would fry the spices with the poultry to take the raw edge off my freshly-ground cumin and to give the poultry some color (it never browned despite adding extra fat). Thank you jeidipippins for sharing your recipe.

I've made this many times and finally decided to review it. This last time I made a few additions which I think made this dish even better. First I always double the recipe as it never lasts long and it's great as a leftover, so remember the following is for a double batch. In place of the tomato sauce I use a 28 oz. can of petite diced tomatoes drained (save the liquid)and a 6 oz. can of tomato paste. I use 1 cup of the small pimento stuffed olives measured after chopping. In addition to the raisins I add a 4.5 oz. box of pitted prunes chopped. A yellow or red bell pepper in place of the green. Add 1 cup of the liquid from the drained tomatoes to a small pot with 1/2 cup of Quinoa and cook as directed. Once cook add to the other ingredients in Step 2 along with a small can of chopped Portobello mushrooms. I like mine spicey but do as others have suggested and add the cayenne a little at a time or eliminate and use Rotel diced tomatoes with green chillis.

My family is from the Dominican republic so I grew up eating picadillo made with ground beef. I don’t purchase ground beef in my home (I use ground turkey for everything) so when I found this recipe I was thrilled to try it. I must say it is absolutely easy and delicious!! I’ve been making this for years now—and quite often at least once a month—my husband and two kids (they were ages 2&3 when I started giving this to them) ALWAYS ask for seconds. I do double most of the recipe (2LBS of turkey and one full can of beans), omit the spice bc of kids, and have a nice amount of leftovers, which everyone loves. Deliciosa, sabrosa receta Caribeña/Cubana. FIVE STARS!

This is a delicious recipe. I have had better, but not sure what the difference was. This is a keeper though and I will be putting this in my dinner rotation. Next time i will probably use more olives and raisins. Possibly forgo the black beans or use chili beans instead. It tastes great as-is though

I've made this twice in the last 2 months during our Shelter in Place.
It's sooo good and easy! I served it with quinoa and corn. 

The second time I made it, I used the whole can of black beans. It gave the Picadillo at little more substance for the two men in my family.
Great recipe, so rich and flavorful! Husbo didn't even know it was turkey. I added few packets of Sazon, and extra olives, capers and raisins. So yummy!

ITS DELICIOUS!!! I could not believe how healthy is it compared to such big flavor. My kids asked me to make it every week, and I sure will. The only thing I would change is adding less cayenne pepper, it was too spicy for the kids. I'd recommend just adding half the serving. Oh! Also, I like more raisins in it too. You will love it!

i did a lot of different things to this but the main concept was kept..... thats why i gave it 5 stars cause its SO versatile... i used garbanzo beans,added a can of diced tomatoes, peas and believe it or not i diced a sweet potato and threw that in there also!!! EVERYBODY had seconds....and it was healthy so you dont feel guilty!! wonderful staple

Delicious! I had never heard of Picadillo and stumbled upon this recipe when looking for something utilizing ground turkey - what a find! My whole family loved it!! I did reduce the cayenne to 1/4 tsp for my kids taste, but it still had a little kick, and it already has a lot of flavor from the other ingredients. I also added a can of drained chopped tomatoes and served it over brown rice. This is definitely a keeper and will be made again and again. Thank you!!!

This is delicious... the only thing that I would change to give it 5 stars would be to add more raisins (double them) and olives and less cayenne. I used one tbsp and it was way to spicy. I ate it plain and it was good alone.
So yummy! I did not change the recipe and it was perfect!
Easy mid week meal, quick and so tasty
This was delicious! I will make again and again! Such a fun and a wat
Way too spicy.
I will agree with the other commentors, thought I could handle the spice but 2 tsp of each is a bit much. Still able to eat it and enjoy it, but I'll be doing a little less spice next time
Love it!!! my husband asked me to make sure I save the recipe. He wants me to make this again. Next time I will add the Cheyenne and the olive brine.
Delicious, easy! Completely forgot the cayenne and didnt miss it but next time will add. First helping used it on hamburger rolls but liked it much better on its own.
I enjoyed this "Turkey Picadillo II"; however, I had issues trying to brown the turkey (the way hubby likes it). Thank you jeidipippins for sharing your recipe.
This is excellent. Hubby loved it in tortilla shells.
